problem:
What is the geometrical interpretation of the transformation represented by the matrix $A$ given below? 
 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2\sqrt{3}} & -\frac{1}{2} \\ \frac{1}{2} & \frac{3}{2\sqrt{3}}\end{aligned}]
$$

choices.value: A rotation of $\frac{\pi }{3}$ radians counterclockwise about the origin.
A rotation of $\frac{\pi }{6}$ radians counterclockwise about the origin.
A rotation of $\frac{\pi }{6}$ radians clockwise about the origin.
A rotation of $\frac{\pi }{3}$ radians clockwise about the origin.
A rotation of $\frac{7\pi }{6}$ radians counterclockwise about the origin.
